title_en: Zou v. Gao, Sun, and Chen — dispute over statutory inheritance
ruling_gist_en: In a divorce, if one party as a stepparent explicitly states that they will no longer support and educate their stepchildren whom they have previously supported and educated, it shall be deemed that the stepparent-stepchild relationship is dissolved by agreement from that point. When the stepparent dies, the stepchildren whose relationship has already been dissolved cannot claim statutory inheritance of the stepparent's estate on the grounds that they fall under the circumstance of 'stepchildren who have a fostering relationship' as provided in the Inheritance Law; the people's court will not support such a claim.
keywords_en: civil; legal inheritance dispute; second instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; natural person; inheritance law; right of inheritance after dissolution of stepparent-stepchild relationship; determination of fostering relationship; qualification as statutory heir; partial support; divorce; fostering of stepchildren; statutory inheritance; will; Chen's legal inheritance dispute
full_text_en:
Zou Moulei v. Gao Moumou, Sun Mou, Chen Mou — dispute over statutory succession

Ruling Summary

In a divorce, if a stepparent clearly indicates that he or she will no longer support a stepchild whom he or she has raised and educated, this shall be deemed as the dissolution of the stepparent-stepchild relationship from that time. Where the stepparent dies, and the stepchild whose relationship has already been dissolved claims statutory inheritance of the stepparent's estate on the ground that they fall within the category of "stepchildren with a supporting relationship" as provided in the Succession Law, the people's court shall not support such a claim.

Plaintiff: Zou Moulei, female, 45 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Defendants:
- Gao Moumou, female, 44 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Huangpu District, Shanghai.
- Sun Mou, female, 15 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Huangpu District, Shanghai.
- Legal representative: Gao Moumou, mother of Sun Mou.
- Chen Mou, male, 37 years old, Han ethnicity, originally domiciled in Hongkou District, Shanghai, currently residing in the United States.

Plaintiff Zou Moulei filed a lawsuit with the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai against defendants Gao Moumou, Sun Mou, and Chen Mou concerning a dispute over statutory succession.

Plaintiff's Allegations:

The decedent Sun Moumou and the third-party Zou Moujuan gave birth to a daughter after their marriage, who is the plaintiff Zou Moulei (formerly named Sun Moulei). In September 1981, Sun Moumou and Zou Moujuan divorced by court mediation, and Zou Moulei lived with Zou Moujuan. Thereafter, Sun Moumou remarried the third-party Chen Moumou. Defendant Chen Mou is the son of Chen Moumou from her previous marriage. Later, Sun Moumou remarried defendant Gao Moumou, and they had a daughter, defendant Sun Mou. The disputed house is the personal property registered under the decedent Sun Moumou's name. Sun Moumou died on May 4, 2016, without leaving a will. Therefore, the plaintiff requested that the statutory heirs of Sun Moumou equally inherit the decedent Sun Moumou's estate, i.e., the property house located at Room X, North Xizang Road, Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as the "disputed house").

Defense of Gao Moumou and Sun Mou jointly:

Plaintiff Zou Moulei has no conclusive evidence proving that the decedent Sun Moumou and Zou Moulei are father and daughter. During his lifetime, Sun Moumou only had one daughter, defendant Sun Mou. Defendant Chen Mou also failed to provide conclusive evidence that he was a stepchild with a supporting relationship with the decedent Sun Moumou. Gao Moumou married Sun Moumou in 2002 and took care of Sun Moumou for a long time. Sun Mou, as a minor legitimate daughter, lived with Sun Moumou for a long time. Therefore, they should receive a larger share of the inheritance. Moreover, after Sun Moumou's death, Gao Moumou and Sun Mou applied for and obtained an inheritance notarization, and through Notarial Certificate (2016) Hu Zha Zheng Zi No. 2171, they inherited the disputed house under Sun Moumou's name. Currently, the disputed house is registered with Gao Moumou and Sun Mou each owning a one-half share. Therefore, they oppose Zou Moulei's claim.

Defense of Chen Mou:

After Sun Moumou remarried Chen Moumou in 1984, Chen Mou, as Sun Moumou's stepchild, lived together with Sun Moumou and Chen Moumou at Sun Moumou's registered residence at Room X, North Chongqing Road, Shanghai. In 1991, the divorce agreement between Chen Moumou and Sun Moumou stipulated that Chen Mou, the son of Chen Moumou from her previous marriage, would be raised by Chen Moumou and move back to his original registered residence. As a stepchild, Chen Mou may inherit Sun Moumou's estate, i.e., the ownership of the disputed house, according to law.

Facts Found by the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance:

The decedent Sun Moumou and Zou Moujuan registered their marriage in March 1974. On December 22, 1974, they had a daughter named Sun Moulei, later renamed Zou Moulei, who is the plaintiff in this case. Sun Moumou and Zou Moujuan divorced by mediation of the Changji City People's Court of Xinjiang on September 28, 1981. Sun Moumou remarried Chen Moumou on December 8, 1984. After the marriage, Chen Mou, the son of Chen Moumou from her previous marriage, lived together with Sun Moumou at Room X, North Chongqing Road, Shanghai. On October 17, 1991, Sun Moumou and Chen Moumou divorced by agreement. Thereafter, Sun Moumou remarried Liu Moumou, had no children from that marriage, and divorced by agreement on November 16, 2000. On May 16, 2002, Sun Moumou registered marriage with defendant Gao Moumou, and they had a daughter named Sun Mou. Sun Moumou died on May 3, 2016. Both of his parents predeceased him.

It was also found that the disputed house underwent ownership registration in 2000, with Sun Moumou registered as the owner. After Sun Moumou's death on May 3, 2016, defendants Gao Moumou and Sun Mou applied to the Shanghai Zhabei Notary Public Office for inheritance notarization on May 9, 2016. Subsequently, Notarial Certificate (2016) Hu Zha Zheng Zi No. 2171 (issued on August 22, 2016) confirmed that the disputed house would be jointly inherited by Gao Moumou and Sun Mou. On August 23, 2016, Gao Moumou and Sun Mou applied to change the ownership registration of the disputed house. On September 5, 2016, the registration of the disputed house was approved to be changed to Gao Moumou and Sun Mou each owning a one-half share.

During the trial, Sun Mouzhong, the brother of the decedent Sun Moumou, testified in court: Plaintiff Zou Moulei is the daughter of Sun Moumou and Zou Moujuan. After Sun Moumou remarried Chen Moumou, Sun Moumou, Chen Moumou, and defendant Chen Mou, the son of Chen Moumou from her previous marriage, lived together at Room X, North Chongqing Road, Shanghai. After Sun Moumou and Chen Moumou divorced, both Chen Moumou and Chen Mou moved away. After Sun Moumou remarried Liu Moumou, they had no children, and no children lived with them.

Opinion of the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai at First Instance:

Estate is the lawful personal property left by a citizen at death, and citizens have the right to inherit property according to law. The disputed house in this case is a property house originally registered under the name of the decedent Sun Moumou. The decedent Sun Moumou did not leave a will during his lifetime. Therefore, his estate, i.e., the disputed house, shall be jointly inherited by his statutory heirs. Plaintiff Zou Moulei, as the daughter of Sun Moumou and his former wife Zou Moujuan; defendant Chen Mou, as a stepchild with a supporting relationship with Sun Moumou; defendant Gao Moumou, as the spouse of Sun Moumou; and defendant Sun Mou, as the legitimate daughter of Sun Moumou, may all inherit the ownership of the disputed house as first-order statutory heirs of Sun Moumou.

Accordingly, the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Articles 2, 3, and 5 of the Succession Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on September 14, 2017:

The ownership of the house located at Room X, North Xizang Road, Shanghai, which belongs to the estate of the decedent Sun Moumou and is registered under the names of defendants Gao Moumou and Sun Mou, shall be held in common by plaintiff Zou Moulei and defendants Gao Moumou, Sun Mou, and Chen Mou, with each entitled to a one-fourth share. Zou Moulei, Gao Moumou, Sun Mou, and Chen Mou shall jointly go through the procedures for changing the ownership registration of the said house within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment, and they have the obligation to cooperate with each other. The expenses incurred in changing the ownership registration of the said house shall be borne by Zou Moulei, Gao Moumou, Sun Mou, and Chen Mou respectively according to law.

Gao Moumou and Sun Mou, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, arguing:

The first-instance judgment was unclear in its findings of fact. First, there is no evidence in this case proving that Zou Moulei is a lawful heir. Moreover, the procedure for witness Sun Mouzhong to testify in court was unlawful; he did not submit a written application or was summoned to testify. In fact, Sun Mouzhong had no contact with the decedent Sun Moumou, and their relationship was broken; thus, the validity of his testimony cannot be recognized and should not be used as evidence in the lawsuit. Second, the first-instance judgment's finding as to whether Chen Mou had a supporting relationship with Sun Moumou was unclear. In fact, when Chen Mou was a minor, his mother Chen Moumou divorced Sun Moumou, and Sun Moumou explicitly stated that he would no longer support Chen Mou. Thereafter, Chen Mou lived with his mother Chen Moumou and resided abroad, having no further contact with Sun Moumou. Therefore, Chen Mou cannot be recognized as a stepchild with a supporting relationship with the decedent Sun Moumou and should no longer enjoy the inheritance rights of a stepchild. Third, the first-instance judgment also failed to consider that Sun Mou is a minor with special difficulties in life and lack of labor capacity, and that Gao Moumou had taken care of the decedent Sun Moumou for a long time, so it was improper not to award her a larger share of the inheritance. Accordingly, they requested that the first-instance judgment be set aside and the case remanded for retrial or amended so that the two appellants each own a one-half share of the house at Room X, North Xizang Road, Shanghai.

Zou Moulei argued:

The evidence provided in the first instance sufficiently proves that she is Sun Moulei, the daughter born to the decedent Sun Moumou and Zou Moujuan in 1974. She later changed her name to Zou Moulei for the convenience of schooling. Therefore, her status as a lawful heir cannot be denied, and Zou Moulei should enjoy the right of inheritance. She objects to Gao Moumou and Sun Mou's request to deny Zou Moulei's status as a lawful heir.

Chen Mou argued:

The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and the evidence was reliable. He requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

During the second instance, the court, ex officio, obtained from the Exit-Entry Administration Bureau of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau Chen Mou's entry-exit records from 1998 when he went abroad to August 24, 2018. The records are as follows: Chen Mou entered the country on January 26, 2003, and departed on March 10 of the same year; entered on February 7, 2007, and departed on February 27 of the same year; entered on May 20, 2009, and departed on May 27 of the same year.

It was further found that the "Voluntary Divorce Agreement" registered and filed by the decedent Sun Moumou and Chen Mou's mother Chen Moumou at the civil affairs bureau on July 1, 1991, stipulated:

"1. Child Support: The boy, Chen Mou, born to the woman from her previous marriage, ... shall still be raised by the woman until he works, and the man shall not bear other expenses. ... 3. Accommodation Arrangements: The woman and her son (Chen Mou) shall move back to their original registered residence, and the man shall reside at his registered residence. After the divorce, the man shall live at Room X, North Chongqing Road, with his household registration at the same address. The woman shall live at Room X, Zhoujiazui Road, with her household registration at the same address."

Opinion of the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court:

Regarding the disputed issue of whether Chen Mou meets the requirement of being a stepchild who formed a supporting relationship with the decedent under the Succession Law, the court makes the following evaluation. Pursuant to Article 10 of the Succession Law, whether step-parents and stepchildren enjoy inheritance rights depends on whether a supporting relationship has been formed. When step-parents and stepchildren have actually formed a supporting relationship, the direct affinity by marriage transforms into a fictitious blood relationship, thereby giving rise to legally fictitious rights and obligations between parents and children. The determination of whether a supporting relationship has been formed should take the time when the inheritance actually occurs as the node. In this case, when Chen Mou was two years old, due to the marriage of his biological mother Chen Moumou to the decedent Sun Moumou, he indeed lived together with Sun Moumou, forming a de facto stepfather-stepson relationship. Sun Moumou and Chen Moumou jointly raised and educated Chen Mou. Later, Chen Moumou and Sun Moumou divorced by agreement. According to Article 13 of the "Specific Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Child Support in Divorce Cases by People's Courts" (November 3, 1993): "After the biological father and stepmother or the biological mother and stepfather divorce, if the stepfather or stepmother does not agree to continue supporting the stepchild who was previously raised and educated by them, the child shall still be supported by the biological parents." The court holds that the relationship between step-parents and stepchildren is a de facto supporting relationship arising from affinity. This relationship is legally fictitious. After divorce, if the step-parent is unwilling to continue supporting, it shall be deemed that the step-parent-stepchild relationship is dissolved, and the rights and obligations between them as parents and children cease to exist. In this case, Chen Mou was once supported by Sun Moumou. However, at the time of the divorce between his biological mother Chen Moumou and Sun Moumou, Chen Mou was nine years old and still a minor. Moreover, Sun Moumou and Chen Moumou explicitly agreed in the divorce agreement that Chen Mou would continue to be raised by Chen Moumou and that Sun Moumou would no longer bear support expenses. Under these circumstances, it shall be determined that Sun Moumou's discontinuation of support constituted a termination of the previously formed supporting fact, and the stepfather-stepson relationship between Sun Moumou and Chen Mou was deemed dissolved. Furthermore, after the dissolution of the stepfather-stepson relationship between Chen Mou and Sun Moumou until Sun Moumou's death from illness, more than twenty years had passed, and the two had no further contact. Chen Mou went abroad in 1998 and returned to China only three times, staying for short periods. After reaching adulthood, he also did not fulfill the obligation of supporting Sun Moumou. Therefore, the court holds that although a supporting fact existed between Chen Mou and the decedent Sun Moumou, because Sun Moumou no longer supported Chen Mou after divorcing Chen Mou's biological mother Chen Moumou, and because Chen Mou did not perform the duty of support after reaching adulthood, at the time of the inheritance occurrence, the stepfather-stepson relationship between Chen Mou and the decedent Sun Moumou had been dissolved, and the rights and obligations between them no longer existed. Chen Mou does not meet the requirement of being a stepchild with a supporting relationship under the Succession Law. In summary, Chen Mou does not have the right to inherit the estate of the decedent Sun Moumou. The first-instance judgment's determination that Chen Mou was a statutory heir was improper and is corrected according to law.

Estate is the lawful personal property left by a citizen at death, and citizens have the right to inherit property according to law. When inheritance begins, if there is no will, it shall be handled in accordance with statutory succession. The first-instance judgment, based on the evidence in the record and the witness testimony of Sun Mouzhong given in court during the first-instance trial, determined that Zou Moulei is the daughter of the decedent Sun Moumou and his former wife Zou Moujuan, and listed her as a statutory heir. This finding is not improper and is confirmed. In this case, the disputed house is a property house originally registered under the name of the decedent Sun Moumou. The decedent Sun Moumou did not leave a will during his lifetime, so his estate shall be handled according to statutory succession. Zou Moulei, as the daughter of Sun Moumou and his former wife Zou Moujuan; Gao Moumou, as the spouse of Sun Moumou; and Sun Mou, as the legitimate daughter of Sun Moumou and Gao Moumou, shall all inherit the ownership of the disputed house as first-order statutory heirs of Sun Moumou according to law. At the same time, considering that Gao Moumou lived together with Sun Moumou for a long time and performed the primary obligation of supporting the decedent, she may appropriately receive a larger share when distributing the estate according to law. In summary, some of the appeal claims of Gao Moumou and Sun Mou are established and shall be supported according to law. The first-instance judgment's determination that Chen Mou was a statutory heir is improper and is corrected.

Accordingly, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 10 of the Succession Law of the People's Republic of China and Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on October 31, 2018:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2016) Hu 0106 Min Chu No. 18925 of the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai;

2. The ownership of the house located at Room X, North Xizang Road, Shanghai, which belongs to the estate of the decedent Sun Moumou and is registered under the names of Gao Moumou and Sun Mou, shall be held in common by Zou Moulei, Gao Moumou, and Sun Mou, with Zou Moulei enjoying a 30% share, Gao Moumou enjoying a 40% share, and Sun Mou enjoying a 30% share. Zou Moulei, Gao Moumou, and Sun Mou shall jointly go through the procedures for changing the ownership registration of the house at the said address within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment. Zou Moulei, Gao Moumou, and Sun Mou have the obligation to cooperate with each other. The expenses incurred in changing the ownership registration of the house at the said address shall be borne by Zou Moulei, Gao Moumou, and Sun Mou in proportion.

This judgment is final.
